title: the wiring links missing verbs, not only missing directories
why: Today 'a new verb is reachable' is enforced by whoever remembers to delete an instance bin directory or make a symlink by hand. That is policy where it should be physics (Law 4), and it bites immediately: ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin holds one hand-placed file, so the wiring skips the cairn device forever and `cairn restart` would land in a class bin nothing ever links. The same missing precision leaves `cairn cc restart spawn N` standing up a tmux session and a flags home for instance N with no ~/.cairn/devices/cc/N/bin behind them.
how: cairn/devices/recovery/bootstrap.sh holds both halves. `_cairn_wire_device` returns early when the instance bin DIRECTORY exists; `_cairn_wire_single` beside it already has the per-FILE rule (link what is missing, repoint a link that points elsewhere, leave a real file). Guard the bin that IS its class bin first, then move the skip from the directory into the per-script loop, name the counts' unit, and let the function take one device and instance. Then bin/cairn, which already sources bootstrap.sh, calls it for the one instance a command addresses when that instance is declared in class-space (outline 5.7.3.4) and its bin is missing or lacks a word the class bin offers: the command lazy-inits (I-the-command-lazy-inits-the-system.md), so no spawn path and no heartbeat needs to remember. THE BUILD SPEC IS THE `decisions` LIST.
traces_to: Law 4 -- a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. Also Law 1: the recipe was compiled once (ticket 0853294fe972 lifted it whole so it would have one address and no copy); a verb that silently fails to appear makes the next mind re-derive why.

clauses.claim: a class verb added under an already-wired real-directory instance bin is linked by the wiring, and a link that already points at its class verb is not rewritten (its lstat mtime is unchanged)
an instance bin that IS its class bin (a whole-directory symlink) is left alone: the class bin's listing is unchanged and holds no self-pointing link
a hand-placed regular file where a class verb would link stays byte-identical, is counted left, and its path is printed on stderr

cairn_wire_instances <device> <instance> wires only that device's instance bin with the names instance 0 gets, touching no other device or instance; a non-numeric instance or an unknown device is refused nonzero and creates nothing
the counts line names its unit, 'linked N already M left K', the numbers add up to the class verbs walked, and bootstrap_first_run.sh no longer calls them devices

cairn <device>.<n> <word>, where class-space declares cairn/devices/<device>/<n>/ and instance-space has no bin for it, wires that bin before dispatch and the word reaches it; a class verb missing from an existing instance bin is linked the first time it is asked for; an undeclared instance still refuses 'no such instance' and nothing is created for it

constraints.text: Nothing here is fatal except a refused argument: every ln stays `|| true` and the full walk returns 0 against an unwritable instance root.
Idempotent: a second run over a fully wired device rewrites nothing.
STALE LINKS ARE NOT PRUNED and a real file is never overwritten: instance-space has no undo (bin/cmd/deletegate).
The per-file rule is COPIED from `_cairn_wire_single`, not invented.

intention: The instance wiring links every class-space verb that has no instance link yet, instead of only wiring devices whose instance bin does not exist at all -- and it wires the instance a spawn just created, not only instance 0.

decisions.text: D1: In `_cairn_wire_device` (bootstrap.sh), before any write: when `readlink -f` of the instance bin equals `readlink -f` of the class bin and the class side is non-empty, count every executable in the class bin `already` and return 0, writing nothing. FIRST, because 6 of today's instance bins (cc, harbor_master, inference_domain, librarian, tester, trouble) are whole-directory links into the repo, and a per-file `ln -sf` under one would commit a self-pointing link into class-space.

D2: The directory skip is deleted and the per-script loop decides per file, as `_cairn_wire_single` does: a link already resolving to its class verb is `already` and untouched; a link resolving elsewhere or dangling is repointed with `ln -sfn` and counted `linked`; a missing name is linked; a real non-link file is left, counted `left`, and its path printed on stderr ('hand-placed file stands where class verb <name> would link: <path>'). Only `-f -x` files are linked, in both helpers (`_cairn_wire_single` skips a script_path that is not an executable file). `mkdir -p` runs only when there is something to link.

D3: The counters become `linked already left` (replacing `wired skipped`) in the `local` line, both helpers, the boot-log line (`wire: linked=.. already=.. left=.. root=..`) and the echo (`linked N already M left K`). bootstrap_first_run.sh line 72 prints the line as is, without the word 'device(s)'. No proof reads the old words (grep 2026-11-09: codemother test_launcher_words_are_scripts.py and recovery test_launchers_moved_to_their_devices.py call the wiring but read no counts).

D4: cairn_wire_instances [<device> <instance>]: with no arguments the full walk runs as today (superclaude, then every cairn/devices/*/0/bin at instance 0). With two, only $CAIRN_REPO_ROOT/cairn/devices/<device>/0/bin is walked into <instance_root>/<device>/<instance>/bin; superclaude is untouched (wired only by the full walk). The instance must match ^[0-9]+$ and the device must have a class bin; otherwise one line on stderr names the bad argument and the function returns 1 having created nothing; one argument alone is the same refusal. The recovery charter cairn/devices/recovery/intention+why.json gains the string "cairn_wire_instances (bootstrap.sh)" in its public_interface list, because bin/cairn calls it. To write it: load the charter's JSON, append that string, dump it (indent 2, ensure_ascii False, trailing newline) to ~/.akien/temp/recovery_charter.json, then run: bin/cairn artifact write cairn/devices/recovery/intention+why.json --verb cast --why 'bin/cairn calls cairn_wire_instances (ticket f0ffa0db0952)' --from ~/.akien/temp/recovery_charter.json ; then run cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/recompile_gate.sh (it exists: the model compiler's one write-door).

D5: bin/cairn, right after `device_bin=` is computed: let `class_bin=$HERE/../cairn/devices/$device/0/bin` and `want` be the folded first word, or the device name when there is none or it starts with '-'. When `$HERE/../cairn/devices/$device/$instance` is a directory (the instance is declared, outline 5.7.3.4) and class_bin is a directory, and either device_bin is not a directory or (`$class_bin/$want` is executable and `$device_bin/$want` does not exist), source `$HERE/../cairn/devices/recovery/bootstrap.sh` and run `CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT="$INSTANCE_ROOT" cairn_wire_instances "$device" "$instance" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`; dispatch then proceeds unchanged. An undeclared instance meets none of this and reaches the existing 'no such instance' refusal. This replaces the cast D5's call from cc's restart `cmd_spawn`: the command that needs the bin makes it.

D6: recovery's proof, cairn/devices/recovery/proofs/test_instance_wiring_links_every_verb.py, PROVES {'f0ffa0db0952': {'1'..'5'}}, one tooth per clause 1-5. Each tooth builds a scratch repo through cairn.tools.scratch.scratch.scratch_dir holding a COPY of bootstrap.sh at cairn/devices/recovery/ (so CAIRN_REPO_ROOT, derived from its own path, is the scratch repo) and a fixture device's cairn/devices/<dev>/0/bin with executable stubs, and a scratch CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT; it runs `bash -c 'source "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; cairn_wire_instances "${@:2}"'`. Never ~/.cairn, never the live repo. Teeth assert invariants (a link resolves to its class stub; a listing is unchanged; linked+already+left equals the stubs walked), never pinned counts.

D7: bin's proof, bin/proofs/test_a_declared_instance_is_wired_by_the_command.py, PROVES {'f0ffa0db0952': {'6'}}. It copies bin/cairn and cairn/devices/recovery/bootstrap.sh into a scratch repo with a fixture device declared at instances 0 and 2 whose class bin has a stub verb printing $0, sets CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT to a scratch root holding cairn/0, and runs the copied bin/cairn: `<dev>.2 stub` prints the scratch instance-2 path; a second stub added to the class bin is reached through instance 0's existing real bin; `<dev>.5 stub` exits 127 naming 'no such instance' and no <dev>/5 exists after.

out: cc's restart (the cast D5's spawn caller is replaced by D5's lazy wiring)
harbor_master's bin (under cairn/devices/cairn/machines/, not walked by the device loop)
~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/bin/cairn (the hand-placed file is left and reported, never replaced)

measured.saw: class bins: cc{cc,restart} codemother{codemother,cross,question,seed,show,watch} inference_domain librarian{ask,librarian} operator{answer,operator,show} tester trouble{clear,drain,live,trouble}; instance bins for cc, harbor_master, inference_domain, librarian, tester, trouble are whole-directory symlinks to their class bin; cairn/0/bin holds one hand-placed regular file 'cairn'; codemother/0/bin and operator/0/bin are real directories of correct links; superclaude/0/bin links cairn/devices/cc/superclaude

bin/cairn wires only when ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0 is absent (line 153), and a dotted address whose bin is missing refuses 'no such instance'; _cairn_wire_device returns at its first line when the instance bin is a directory
